fatal_errors: Claims suitability and improved integrity under aggressive high-temperature mechanical service even though no corrosion, wear, aggressive-environment, or service-life testing was performed.
Characterizes the ESD layer as crack-resistant and reduced-residual-stress, whereas multilayer deposition produced pores, roughness, and superficial microfissures, especially after six layers.
Uses fusion welding as the experimental baseline, although the actual comparisons were lower versus higher SPS temperatures and three versus six ESD layers.
Omits the specified HEA compositions, SPS processing windows, C1018 substrate, ESD parameters, and observed six-layer deposition limit.
explanation: The response recovers the broad SPS-electrode plus multilayer-ESD intervention and the general ideas that SPS densifies/homogenizes feedstock and ESD limits bulk heat input while creating a metallurgical coating. However, it generalizes the work into a validated repair for hot-crack-prone components and aggressive service, neither of which was tested. It also reverses an important defect trend: repeated deposition did not simply yield a low-stress, crack-free layer; six layers generally increased oxidation, roughness, pores, and microfissuring. The proposed head-to-head fusion-weld experiment is reasonably discriminating as future work, but it is not supporting evidence for the hypothesis. With no cited evidence and no reconstruction of the actual compositions, process conditions, baselines, or measured outcomes, this is only a partial reconstruction.
